glossaryTab.title: Ontology
glossaryTab.newTermHint: A concept is a business idea that names no column or table yet. Link it to other terms with relationships.
glossaryTab.domainsHint: A concept has no columns to derive its domains from, so name them here. Whoever reaches any one of them may read and curate the term.
glossaryTab.deleteDisabledHint: This term has refs or relationships. Retire it to take it out of service, or move its refs and remove its relationships to delete it.
glossaryTab.flipEdgeLabel: Flip which term is the subject of the new relationship
glossaryTab.excludeFromExportHelp: Some columns carry business data, some carry plumbing. A term like "etl batch identifier" or "row version" has a real definition — it just isn't business vocabulary. Exclude it and it stays here for engineers, out of the catalogs Provisa publishes to. The columns still export; the term and its relationships do not.
glossaryTab.retireHint: Take this term out of service: it keeps its columns, but agent term search and metadata export both skip it.
glossaryTab.unretireHint: Put this term back in service.
glossaryTab.proposedUndefined: Proposed: derived from the column and table names. Give it a definition — that is what agents and catalogs read. The name comes from the columns below, and columns that normalize alike land on one term: alias a column on the Tables page to change which term it feeds. Rename here to change only this term's wording.
glossaryTab.proposedUngrounded: Proposed: this term reaches no physical column. Relate it to a term that has one so it names real data.
glossaryTab.purposeBody: It is how people and agents find the right data and use it correctly. Each term names one business concept, lists every physical column that carries it, and says what it actually means — so a question asked in business language lands on the right column instead of a plausible-looking wrong one.
glossaryTab.purposeAdd: Terms for real columns are derived for you. Add one by hand only for a concept no single column carries — an umbrella term you then relate to the terms that do, so it still reaches real data.
glossaryTab.readOnlyHint: You can read the ontology but not curate it. Curating terms, definitions and relationships needs the glossary_rw capability.
glossaryTab.roleHelp_class: Grounded in tables: it names what each of their rows is.
glossaryTab.roleHelp_property: Grounded in columns: it names what their values are.
glossaryTab.roleHelp_concept: Grounded in neither tables nor columns.
glossaryTab.groundedTablesPlaceholder: Tables whose rows this term names
glossaryTab.domainsDerived: Derived from its columns and tables
glossaryTab.derivedReason: Role, Proposed and Deprecated follow from the term's columns, tables, definition and relationships, so they are not set here.
glossaryTab.claimHint: Each column belongs to one term; claiming it moves it here.
glossaryTab.groundDisabled: This term names columns (a property); a class term can't also own columns
glossaryTab.danglingHelp: Connected to no term that names a table or column: it names no data yet.
glossaryTab.classKeys: Keys follow from its tables and declared relationships
glossaryTab.keyColumnClaim: This column is a key; it belongs to its table's class
glossaryTab.findingMessage_unlinked_tables: Grounded in several tables not yet linked as the same entity: mark same-entity relationships between them
glossaryTab.findingMessage_class_and_attribute: Grounded in tables and naming columns at once: a term is a class or an attribute, not both
glossaryTab.findingMessage_tag_wrong_kind: Carries a tag meant for another kind of object
glossaryTab.findingMessage_retirement_blocked: Its columns or tables have nowhere to go: retiring it needs a successor
glossaryTab.findingMessage_no_data: Names no column and is grounded in no table
